Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr
Data serialization methods via S-expressions. Taken from a mix of R7RS, Racket and Perl syntax.

S-expressions are modeled under three classes (Atom, Cons, Nil), belonging to two categories (atom and list), overlapping at exactly Nil.

  • Consider an S-expression as binary tree: an atom is a terminal node; it either has a value (Atom) or it doesn’t (Nil).
  • A cons, modeled by the Cons class, is an internal node with two children, car and cdr (pronounced cou-der). Because cons is derived from the verb construct, and pluralizing it would leave the impression of a verb, it is customary to call it by the somewhat redundant names cons cell or cons pair.
  • In S-expressions, a list is a chain of zero or more cons cells, terminated by Nil. The interpretation of cons cells in the context of lists favors treating the car as the first element (head) of the list, and cdr as the rest. One may traverse the list by reading the car and replacing the list with the cdr. The end of list is reached when the list is replaced with Nil, the list terminator. For this reason, Nil is also considered a list—namely the empty list.
